sentence: This project tries to find the missing cellular protein or pathway that an accessory protein of HIV changes to boost the virus's infectivity.
This project tests a CRISPR gene therapy in mice that edits the mutant copy of a gene linked to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia.
This project studies how glycans in mucus trap and neutralize influenza virus in human airway cell models.
This project studies island populations of mice to find out how body size, behavior and recombination evolve.
This project builds a gene therapy that tries to snip HIV out of infected cells in the brain.
This project tests whether drugs given to preterm infants keep the ductus arteriosus, a fetal blood vessel, from closing.
This project studies how sensory neurons in the colon respond to inflammation and develop mechanical hypersensitivity.
This project builds artificial intelligence tools that use nuclear medicine imaging to help characterize cancer.
This project tests whether fluorescence imaging with indocyanine green can quickly and accurately diagnose necrotizing soft-tissue infections.
This project studies the molecular and cellular origins of stem cells that are activated during colonic injury and inflammation.
This project develops ways to link somatic alterations to cellular genealogy to find what shapes cell evolution in normal aging and leukemic transformation.
This project studies how drinking ethanol during adolescence affects astrocytes and their control of synapses in the cortex.
This project develops mass spectrometry tools and noninvasive sampling methods to study lipid regulation across the lifespan.
This project studies how a probiotic engineered to make a cytokine protects the hematopoietic system from ionizing radiation damage.
This project studies how lingering negative emotions and childhood trauma affect the mental, physical and immune health of spouses caring for people with dementia.
This project develops nitrogen-15 labeled probes that let magnetic resonance imaging track how the body uses glutamine.
This project tests whether drugs that block DNA damage checkpoint kinases, combined with immune checkpoint inhibition, can fight uterine cancer.
This project studies how the way tumors are implanted into mice changes results in head and neck cancer models.
This project builds a risk scale using radiomic signatures and clinical data to guide safer therapy for lung cancer patients at risk of cardiovascular disease.
This project makes mouse embryonic stem cells from mouse models of human disease to test genome editing therapies.
